newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas remains higher late on cold forecasts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas remains higher late on cold forecasts.

text.p: NYMEX natgas futures remained near session highs Wednesday on cold weather forecasts, but some technical selling prevented February from breaking out of resistance in the low-$2.60s, industry sources said.
At 1415 EST, February was up 17.7 cents at $3.57 per million British thermal units, while March was 12.4 cents higher at $3.12. Most others were up by one to 6.8 cents.

"Short-term I think you have a bullish sentiment. Long-term I think you have a sideways to slightly bearish sentiment," one futures trader said, noting Feb is about $1.20 over the Feb 1996 contract's settlement despite higher stocks.
According to a Reuter poll, withdrawal expectations for tonight's AGA report are mostly in the 110-120 bcf range.

With a number of storage withdrawal limits in place by Northern Illinois Gas, Peoples Gas and Natural Gas Pipeline, most traders said a high AGA number would further boost both the futures and cash markets.
"I think there's enough bullish information in the market to keep both cash and futures strong through at least next Tuesday," a Houston-based trader said.

Technically, traders said February resistance after breaking through today's high of $3.64 would be in the $3.80-3.84 area. Support was seen in the gap between $3.11 and $3.185, with better buying likely in the $2.60s.

Cash prices along the Gulf Coast prices jumped about 30 cents to the $4.20s and $4.30s, with a resurgence of buying interest evident this afternoon, traders said. Midcontinent prices were assessed in the $5.05-5.10 range, though deals were reported done in a much wider range.

Fueling the cash market for the most part were forecasts calling for much colder temperatures in the eastern two-thirds of the U.S. Friday through early next week, with the most bitter temperatures expected in the Northeast.
Separately, Transco said it lowered pressure on its Leidy, Pa., line due to a dehydration obstruction. Firm volumes were unaffected, but the company would not comment on the impact on IT.
NYMEX said 35,626 Hub contracts traded at 1350 EST.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1425 EST.
On the KCBT, February pared gains to $3.36, still up 13 cents, while deferred months were six to eight cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 4.7 cents to 21 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices at Waha gained about 80 cents to the low-$5 area for Thursday delivery.
